language.title: Translation and German: what exists
language.body:

classify.title: Classification: no frontier benchmark found
classify.body:
We found no independent classification benchmark that covers the current models. Three small signals:

  • Invoice decisions (24 cases): Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna both scored 24 of 24. The run cost $0.0095 and $0.0051, about $0.40 and $0.21 per 1,000. DataCamp
  • Feedback labelling (12,000 records, older models): Sonnet 4.6 had the top F1 at 0.829 for $78.69. Grok-4-fast cost $4.79. Sonnet's composite was only 3.7% higher. Read from a search summary, because the study page refused our fetch.
  • Reading: label a few hundred of your own items and test the cheapest models first. Small models often reach the ceiling on clear rules.

insights.hint: In Reasoning, click the highest dot on the chart.
insights.x: Gemini 4 Carbon tops Intelligence Index v5 at 59, and Google so far offers it only to a subset of cyber defenders and trusted partners. Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 is the best row you can actually buy.

insights.hint: In Reasoning, look at a model with very cheap tokens and a surprisingly high bill.
insights.x: Gemini 3.8 Flash has list prices of $0.75 / $3.75 and costs $7.77 per Index task for 31 points. GPT-6.1 Sol charges $2 / $10 and costs $1.27 for 55 points. Token volume decides the bill.

insights.hint: In Reasoning, compare the two small models at max effort.
insights.x: Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna both list at $0.10 / $0.50. At max effort, Haiku costs $0.41 for 36 points and Luna $0.15 for 28. Equal list prices do not mean equal costs.

insights.hint: In Reasoning, follow the top rung of a premium model.
insights.x: Fable 5.1 drops from 50 at xhigh ($10.85) to 49 at max ($12.99). ARC-AGI-2 shows the same for Opus 5.5: 93.3% at high for 41 cents, 91.7% at max for $1.85. The top rung is not always the top score.

insights.t: Same score, six times the bill
insights.hint: In Reasoning, find a 35-point row and look for its twin.
insights.x: Opus 5.5 at low and GPT-6.1 Sol at low both score 35. Opus costs $0.98 and Sol $0.16. Low effort spends a premium model's strengths on work that does not need them.

insights.t: Half the list price, same bill
insights.hint: In Reasoning, check Sonnet 5.5 at its top rung.
insights.x: Sonnet 5.5 lists at half of Opus 5.5. At max effort, it costs $10.02 per task against $10.04, and scores 54 against 58. At xhigh, Sonnet is back to $4.09 for 50.

insights.hint: In Code, on Terminal-Bench 4.0, click the dot that costs the most at the top.
insights.x: Sonnet 5.5 at max uses about 565k output tokens per Terminal-Bench 4.0 task: $22.22 for 61.8%. GPT-6.1 Sol uses 95k: $1.92 for 58.2%. Both list at $2 / $10, so the difference is token volume alone.

insights.t: The same score at a fifth of the price
insights.hint: In Code, on Terminal-Bench 4.0, look for two rows at exactly the same score.
insights.x: GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra both resolve 58.18% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at max effort. Astra costs $9.90 per task and Sol $1.92.

insights.hint: In Code, on Terminal-Bench 4.0, click the top row and read the notes.
insights.x: Anthropic reports 70.6% for Sonnet 5.5 in its launch post, and the public Terminal-Bench 4.0 board shows 61.8%. Opus 5.5 reads 66.4% against 64.85%. Setups differ, so prefer the board for comparisons.
Low-cost models top CyberGym at 88 to 95%, and Anthropic retired it from its system card "due to saturation". When everyone is near the ceiling, a benchmark stops separating models.

insights.hint: In Security, read the ExploitBench notes.
insights.x: Cyber scores are usually taken with production safeguards off. What you buy may refuse or hand off the same work. Opus 5.5 blocks vulnerability discovery in compiled binaries, for example.

insights.t: People still win, at a price
insights.x: A human panel solves all of ARC-AGI-2 at about $17 per task. GPT-6.1 Sol at max reaches 94.2% for 25 cents. The gap to 100% is small on the score axis and large on the cost axis.

insights.hint: In Computer use, open OSWorld 2.0 and read the notes.
insights.x: Opus 5.5 scores 81.8% on OSWorld 2.0 with partial credit, and 48.7% when every checkpoint of a task must pass. For an agent that must finish the job, the strict number is the one to plan with.

insights.hint: In Classification & extraction, compare GPT-6.1 Sol on perfect documents.
insights.x: GPT-6.1 Sol has 74% value F1 and only 12% perfect documents. Terra medium has nearly the same F1 and 27%. If a single wrong value ruins the document, F1 flatters.

insights.hint: In Classification & extraction, open the classification evidence below the chart.
insights.x: Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna both got 24 of 24 invoice decisions right, for fractions of a cent. Past the ceiling, extra money buys nothing. The sample is small, so test on your own data.

insights.t: The flat end of the curve
insights.hint: In Vision, follow Opus 5.5 to its top rung on Chartography.
insights.x: On Chartography, Opus 5.5 goes from about $0.025 for 59% to about $0.49 for 64%. That is twenty times the cost for five points. Fable 5.1 even falls at its top rung.

missions.brief: Thousands of mixed questions a day. Finance allows $2 per Index-style task. Pick the strongest option that stays inside it.
missions.lesson: GPT-6.1 Sol at max beats Opus 5.5 at medium for half the money, and the cheap-looking Gemini 3.8 Flash costs more than either. Compare per-task costs. List prices tell you little.

missions.brief: Long repository tasks with verifier-checked results. $3 per attempt.
missions.lesson: Gemini 3.8 Flash ties GPT-6 Astra at 74% on DeepSWE for $2.36, yet it resolves only 19% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 for $5.54. One benchmark does not settle a model's value, even within coding.

missions.brief: High volume and simple work. You have 5 cents per task on the same index. How far can you stretch it?
missions.lesson: Haiku 5.5 low and Luna medium land almost level at 4 cents. Terra low has more points but breaks the budget at 7 cents. At this end, the effort setting moves the bill as much as the model does.

missions.brief: One vendor reports 100% on ExploitBench for GPT-6 Astra. Another reports 91% for Claude Opus 5.5. What can you conclude?
choices: Astra is 9 points stronger at exploitation.
Neither score tells you what the API will do: both were taken with safeguards off, by each vendor on its own setup.
Opus 5.5 is safer, because its score is lower.
Both models would refuse this work in production, so the scores mean nothing.
missions.lesson: Each vendor ran its own setup, and Anthropic states that its figures may not compare with public entries. A deployed model may also block the task, so test your own security workload with safeguards on.

missions.brief: Long workflows across real apps. Each run may cost up to $5. Effort levels are shown as rungs: rung 1 is the cheapest.
missions.lesson: Opus 5.5 at rung 4 reaches 80.8% for about $4.25. The top rung adds a single point for twice the money, and Fable 5.1 cannot compete at this budget even though it lists at more than twice the price.

missions.brief: Every wrong value means manual rework, so only perfect documents count. You can spend 25 cents per page.
missions.lesson: Sonnet 5.5 is the best perfect-document rate under the budget. Note that Terra costs five times less for only 5 points fewer, so raising the budget is not always the answer.

missions.brief: Reading charts from reports, without tools. 10 cents per task.
missions.lesson: Opus 5.5 at rung 4 fits the budget and leads by 16 points. Its cheapest rung, at 2 cents, already beats every Fable 5.1 setting. Check the low rungs before paying for more effort.

missions.brief: Gemini 4 Carbon leads the Text Arena at 1528. What does this rating measure?
choices: Which reply people prefer in blind pairwise votes on open chat.
missions.lesson: Preference is real signal for tone and readability, but it does not check facts. Carbon's row is also marked preliminary, and most buyers cannot get the model yet. For translation you need a language-pair test with human review.

missions.brief: Command-line tasks checked by test suites. Each task may cost $8 in its native agent.
missions.lesson: GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 58.18% for $1.92, as much as GPT-6 Astra at max for $9.90. Opus 5.5 leads overall at 64.85%, for $14.30 per task. Whether those 6.7 points are worth seven times the cost depends on the job.

missions.brief: Hard abstract reasoning. 30 cents per task.
missions.lesson: GPT-6.1 Sol at max solves 94.2% for 25 cents. Opus 5.5 at medium costs more and solves 87.5%. Its best setting is high, at 41 cents and 93.3%, and raising effort to max lowers the score.

arc2.name: ARC-AGI-2 Semi-Private

ref.label: Human panel: 100% at about $17 per task

arc2.what: Abstract visual puzzles that resist memorisation. ARC Prize verifies scores on a hidden set and publishes cost per task.
notes: Scores and costs come from the ARC Prize leaderboard data, including rows up to October 2026.
This is one narrow skill, far from everyday engineering.

aacode.name: AA Coding Agent Index v2.0
aacode.what: A composite of FrontierCode v1.1, Terminal-Bench 4.0 and SWE-Atlas-QnA, three attempts per task. Each row is an agent with a model, because the harness affects the result.
notes: Cost is the average pay-per-token API cost per task. Subscriptions change what you actually pay.
Scores without a published cost sit in the strip on the right.
Gemini 4 Carbon runs in the Antigravity CLI and is not generally available.

tb4.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0, native agents
tb4.what: Agents complete 66 command-line tasks in a sandbox, checked by test suites, over 330 trials. Each row runs in its vendor's native agent.
notes: Cost per task is the published total run cost divided by the 330 trials.
Margins are about ±3 points, so GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1 near 58% are a tie.
Vendor figures can differ from the board: Anthropic reports 70.6% for Sonnet 5.5 and 66.4% for Opus 5.5.
tb4.costMethod: Derived from published total_cost_usd / n_trials; not a separately published per-task value.

scoreOnlyEvidence.evidenceExcerpt: On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which evaluates coding agents on realistic, resource-constrained terminal tasks using strict task-specific tests, K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%

deepswe.name: DeepSWE
deepswe.what: Long-horizon software tasks written from scratch across 91 repositories, scored by hand-written verifiers. The same mini agent harness runs every model.
notes: The board was last updated on 22 Sept. Claude 5.5, GPT-6.1 and Gemini 4 are not on it yet.
Margins are ±1 to ±6 points, so GPT-6 Astra and Gemini 3.8 Flash at 74% are a tie.
Artificial Analysis replaced DeepSWE with FrontierCode in its Coding Agent Index v2.0.

arena.name: Text Arena (arena.ai)
arena.what: Blind pairwise preference from 9 million human votes on open chat. It captures how a reply reads, not whether it is correct.
notes: Confidence intervals run ±4 to ±9, so neighbouring rows are ties. Carbon and Gemini 3.8 Flash are preliminary.
Arena has no public per-task cost, so cost is an estimate from list prices.
Rating gaps do not divide: 1500 is not twice 750.

xpro.name: ExtractBench Pro, perfect documents
xpro.what: 100 synthetic long-tail documents, 2,622 pages. A document only counts when every single value matches.
notes: Vendor-run: LlamaIndex sells a competing product. BenchLM mirrors the board and excludes it from its rankings.
Rows run inside coding-agent harnesses, so cost and behaviour reflect the harness too.
The source CSV distinguishes GPT-6.1 Terra Medium and Low; both configurations are displayed with their published labels.

xf1.name: ExtractBench Pro, value F1
xf1.what: The same runs as the perfect-document board, but counting each extracted value on its own.
notes: Vendor-run, same caveats as the perfect-document board.
The source CSV distinguishes GPT-6.1 Terra Medium and Low; both configurations share the runs used by the perfect-document chart.

notes: Elo measures grader preference, not verified correctness.
